decision.summary: The run passes with warnings: no high or critical findings, four medium. The claims are well grounded overall; reading all 177 against full context found one scope error (claim-130 now reads as 70% of all revenue when the figure applied to strategic-initiative revenue on a broad digital-and-AI definition), three low-severity wording issues, and a coverage gap: the NIM-plateau outlook, the Q2 macro-forecast improvement, the TNAV growth expectation and the operating-lease depreciation recovery were not extracted. In the brief, the downside case frames the economy using a superseded Q1 macro cut although management said forecasts improved modestly at H1, and the peer paragraph concludes that Lloyds depends more than its peers on efficiency gains with no peer-plan evidence. Lower-severity points: HSBC's post-event timing is undisclosed, one analyst's view is generalised to 'analysts', and the upside observable is weakly diagnostic. Deterministic gates, injection scan and Jev dispositions are all in order.
